subject: Sea star coral meal
topic: This sea star is slowly eating a coral, working its way up from the bottom.
script:
This sea star is slowly eating a coral, working its way up from the bottom.
Two kilometers down near Johnston Atoll in the Pacific, scientists watched it climb its meal.
Large sea stars like this are among the most common coral predators seen in the deep.
And deep-sea corals can be hundreds, even thousands, of years old.
In the Atlantic, another sea star was caught feeding on a whip coral.
Off the US East Coast, scientists filmed one species eating coral for the very first time.
The scientist who named it had only ever seen it as museum specimens.
Now they had proof that it really is a coral predator.
Would you have guessed sea stars eat coral?
